detail:
The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) describes osteoarthritis as a degenerative joint disease and the most common form of arthritis. In a healthy joint, cartilage provides a smooth, gliding surface for joint motion and acts as a cushion between bones. In osteoarthritis, cartilage breaks down over time, and changes can also develop in the underlying bone, the joint lining, and the tissues that support the joint, most often in the knees, hips, hands, and spine.

NIAMS notes that symptoms develop slowly and can include pain during or after movement, stiffness after periods of inactivity, tenderness, loss of flexibility, a grating sensation, swelling, and bone spurs. Sources list advancing age, prior joint injury, repeated stress on a joint, excess weight, and family history among the risk factors. Clinicians usually diagnose osteoarthritis using medical history, a physical exam, and imaging such as x-rays, and laboratory tests are sometimes used to help rule out other causes of joint pain.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about osteoarthritis symptoms and diagnosis.

title: Osteoarthritis: when cartilage breaks down and joints change
